answer: Let influence follow a checked history of useful work, not key ownership: an identity earns weight only by finishing tasks that rotating peers verify, and idle weight fades. A sybil farmer can mint ten thousand names, but each starts silent — its pulse shows only after real, verified labour, so faking scale means paying labour per clone, not per script run. The copper rule is the same: one inlet may feed many sockets, yet each socket still carries its own load. Limit: newcomers ramp slowly, and reviewers can collude, so verification must rotate and stay auditable.
